transparent.business_two_sentences: JPMorgan Chase is a global financial-services firm earning net interest income from deposit-taking and lending, plus fee income from investment banking, trading, card processing, and asset and wealth management. It reports through four client segments -- Consumer & Community Banking, Corporate & Investment Bank, Commercial Banking, and Asset & Wealth Management -- and returns capital via dividends and buybacks.

claims.text: JPMorgan Chase reported record fourth-quarter 2018 net income of $7.1 billion ($1.98 per diluted share) and record full-year 2018 net income of $32.5 billion ($9.00 per diluted share) [c1].
Full-year 2018 return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) was 17%, versus 14% for the fourth quarter alone [c2].
In the fourth quarter of 2018 the bank opened Chase branches in new states for the first time in nearly a decade, part of a broader push to expand its retail branch footprint [c3].
The bank held the #1 position in global investment-banking fees for 2018 with an 8.7% wallet share, up 60 basis points from the prior year [c4].
Management said the firm grew full-year Markets revenue in the Investment Bank despite a challenging fourth quarter, citing record Equities performance and solid Fixed Income performance [c5].
Fourth-quarter 2018 Markets & Investor Services revenue in the Corporate & Investment Bank was $4.0 billion, down 11% year over year [c6].
Fourth-quarter net income rose 67% year over year, but the prior-year quarter had included a one-time $2.4 billion reduction to net income from the enactment of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act [c7].

The fourth-quarter provision for credit losses rose to $1.5 billion, up $240 million year over year, driven by higher reserve builds in consumer credit card and wholesale Commercial & Industrial portfolios [c8].
Assets under management in the Asset & Wealth Management segment were $2.0 trillion, down 2% year over year on lower market levels [c9].
Home Lending net revenue fell 8% year over year to $1.3 billion on margin compression and lower origination volumes [c10].
Full-year 2018 total net revenue (reported basis) was $109.0 billion versus $100.7 billion in 2017, and full-year net income was $32.5 billion versus $24.4 billion in 2017 [c11].
Full-year 2018 net interest income was $55.1 billion, up 10% from $50.1 billion in 2017 [c12].
Period-end deposits were $1.47 trillion at December 31, 2018, up from $1.44 trillion a year earlier [c13].
Period-end loans, net of the allowance for loan losses, were $971.1 billion at December 31, 2018, up from $917.1 billion a year earlier [c14].
The firm's own financial supplement reported a market capitalization of $319.8 billion at December 31, 2018, down 13% from $366.3 billion a year earlier [c15].

Effective January 1, 2018 the firm adopted new accounting standards applied retrospectively, so 2017 comparative figures shown in the January 2019 release were revised and are not identical to the amounts originally reported in the 2017 Form 10-K [c16].
Full-year 2017 net income had included a $1.9 billion tax expense tied to the estimated impact of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, depressing that year's base for year-over-year comparisons [c17].
The firm-wide provision for credit losses rose 63% from the third to the fourth quarter of 2018 [c18].
The estimated Basel III common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 12.0% at year-end 2018 [c19].
The firm distributed $8.3 billion to shareholders in the fourth quarter of 2018, including $5.7 billion of net share repurchases and a $0.80 per share common dividend [c20].

No formal firm-wide forward revenue or EPS guidance was included in the fourth-quarter 2018 earnings release; JPMorgan Chase does not routinely publish point EPS or revenue guidance the way some non-financial companies do [c21].
Sequential net income fell 16% from the third to the fourth quarter of 2018 as Markets revenue and AWM asset values declined amid the volatile market backdrop [c22].
Full-year noninterest expense rose 7% to $63.4 billion in 2018 from $59.5 billion in 2017 [c23].
